original_question: Given a planar figure, or more generally a body in space, and a distance d > 0, what is the smallest number of points A_1, A_2, ... that can be placed in the region so that every other point A in the region lies within distance d of at least one chosen point?
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core optimization problem: given a planar figure, or more generally a body in space, and a parameter d > 0, choose as few points as possible inside the figure/body so that every point of the figure/body is close to one chosen point. That is exactly the role of item 150, and your wording also correctly keeps the centers inside the region itself. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
missing_details: The paper uses a strict inequality: for every point A in the figure/body, there must exist a chosen point Ai with |AAi| < d, not merely distance at most d or an unspecified notion of “within distance d.” ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
The official formulation says the chosen points A1, A2, ... are themselves included in the given planar figure (or space body). ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

The ambient setting is specifically a planar figure, or more generally a body in space; the paper does not state the problem for arbitrary metric spaces or arbitrary dimensions. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
The universal quantifier is over every other point A included in the same figure/body. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

Nearby context matters: item 149 on the same page is the complementary maximum-points separation problem, so the refined question should stay on the covering side and not drift into the packing version. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
refined_question: Given a planar figure F in the Euclidean plane, or more generally a body B in Euclidean space, and a real number d > 0, determine the minimum cardinality of a set of points {A1, ..., Am} contained in F (respectively in B) such that for every point A in F (respectively in B) there exists an index i with |AAi| < d. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
justification: The nearest official match is item 150, Minimum Points, on page 78. Your draft is already very close to that statement, but the paper’s version is slightly sharper in two ways: it requires the chosen points to be included in the given figure/body, and it uses the strict distance condition |AAi| < d. The immediately preceding item 149 asks for the maximum number of pairwise d-separated points, which confirms that item 150 is the intended covering-type counterpart and should not be broadened into a different optimization problem. The paper gives no added hypotheses such as convexity, smoothness, or higher-dimensional generality beyond “planar figure” / “space body,” so adding such restrictions would move away from the paper’s actual formulation. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
